text:
Alyssa: proposal — small design idea for mixed-capacity pools: introduce a "burst balancer" that actively shifts load into spot lanes up to a safety headroom threshold, then gracefully ramps back to on-demand when interruption risk rises. keeps min-on-demand simple but lets us capture more spot savings in steady periods. thoughts?
Ravi: short version, love it. main question: how do we measure "interruption risk" per region and map that to a headroom percentage?
Mike: we already have a few signals: spot-price trend, preemption rate (5m/1h windows), and cloud provider drain events. combine into a composite score. thresholding like: score < 0.2 -> 80% spot, 0.2-0.5 -> 50% spot, >0.5 -> 20% spot.
Jess: need per-instance-type weighting — some GPU families have catastrophic preemptions during maintenance windows. also tenant SLAs: VIP customers should never go below min_on_demand = X.
Lee: operationally I want this to be reversible quickly. when we see a provider drain, traffic should fall back within 30s to on-demand lanes. otherwise we risk inference errors/timeouts.
Alyssa: agreed. sketch of runtime behavior: 1) continuous scoring, 2) per-cluster spot target from score + configured floor, 3) burst balancer issues small placement policy changes (not full rebalances) to fill spot lanes, 4) on preemption signal or score spike, immediately stop new spot placements and route inflight/queued to on-demand.
Ravi: is there a safe way to avoid a thundering herd when we pull back? e.g., if all spot tasks move to on-demand at once we saturate pods. maybe we use smoothing windows and admission tokens.
Mike: admit tokens + a draining ramp: when switching up, shift 10% of new placements to on-demand every 5s until target met. also keep a warm standby pool of on-demand nodes per region (min_floor) to absorb spikes.
Jess: warm standby costs money. propose we size standby by p99 surge observed in last 30d, but allow a cheaper fallback: short-lived preemptible reserved burst (fast-boot smaller VMs) to buy us 30–90s while we spin up larger on-demand GPUs.
Lee: network concerns: routing between pools needs consistent egress policies and same service account so model downloads/cache hits remain consistent. also watch for cross-AZ bandwidth during simultaneous migrations — that burned us last month.
Alyssa: good call. operational checklist I propose: 
- telemetry: new metric spot_risk_score (0-1) per region+instance-type
- control: burst_balancer config with fields: min_on_demand_floor, warm_standby_size, smooth_window, fallback_policy
- safety: preempt_hook that converts queued->on-demand and marks tenants with eviction_credits
- runbooks: surge-rebalance and slow-fallback steps
Here's a draft config snippet for the balancer:```json
{"burst_balancer": {"min_on_demand_floor": 0.12, "warm_standby_size": 4, "smooth_window_secs": 30, "scale_up_ramp_pct": 10, "fallback_policy": "reserve-short-vms"}}
```
Ravi: eviction_credits idea is nice — let tenants spend credits to avoid eviction during a spot->on-demand panic. credits accrue slowly and can be purchased/assigned for enterprise customers. helps fairness.
Mike: metrics we need to monitor: 1) time-to-fallback (target <30s), 2) on-demand saturation %, 3) observed preemptions avoided, 4) cost delta vs baseline. add alert if fallback time > 60s or on-demand saturation > 85%.
Jess: can we simulate using last 6 months of events? run a replay with our scheduler and measure p99 tail latencies under different scoring thresholds.
Alyssa: yes that's the plan — I can set up a replay job next week. question: anyone object to adding a small default min_on_demand_floor = 10% cluster-level? otherwise some clusters drop to 0 which we've seen cause higher cold-start failures.
Lee: +1 for 10% default, but make it overridable per-tenant.
Ravi: +1. also add a flag to disable for private deployments where customers require strict isolation.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new job queued — infra/replay:bust-balancer-sim at 2321003600 (owner: Alyssa) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Mike: ok next steps: Alyssa to own prototype, Jess to size warm-standby and fallback boot images, Ravi to wire eviction credits, Lee to audit network migration plan. I'll draft the metrics dashboard and alerts.
Alyssa: thanks — I'll post the replay results and a short RFC draft in #eng-infra when ready. :thumbsup:
